stem: Which burn type is characterised by a pink appearance, brisk capillary refill, and blisters?
explanation: Superficial dermal burn is the correct answer because it involves the upper dermis, so perfusion is preserved enough to give brisk capillary refill and blister formation.
rationale: This burn depth usually heals within 10 to 14 days and retains a functioning superficial capillary plexus.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because superficial dermal burns involve the upper dermis, where the capillary plexus remains intact enough to produce brisk capillary refill and blistering.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because epidermal burns are limited to the epidermis and typically cause erythema and pain without blister formation.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because mid-dermal burns are deeper and are more likely to have reduced or absent blanching due to injury to the superficial capillary plexus.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because full thickness burns destroy the full skin thickness, often appearing white, waxy, or charred with no capillary refill.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because deep dermal burns are more severe than superficial dermal burns and usually have impaired capillary refill rather than brisk refill.

source.hint: This depth of burn usually heals within 10 to 14 days and still has a functional superficial capillary plexus.
